summary: Fix integer parsing at signed and unsigned range boundaries.
explanation: The positive accumulator rejects a prefix equal to max/base before examining the next digit. This makes valid values fail: for example, safe_strto8_base("124", &value, 10) is expected to return true and set value to 124, but returns false and leaves value at 127. The same check prevents parsing the valid partial input "123@@@" as 123 and affects positive signed and unsigned boundaries across widths, including the SimpleAtoi, SimpleHexAtoi, leading-substring, and random or exhaustive test failures. The negative accumulator has the parallel problem: it rejects a prefix equal to min/base before the next digit can complete the minimum value. Thus the tested signed minimum strings, including "-128", are expected to parse but return false. Allowing equality through each prefix check lets the existing following-digit overflow check decide whether the completed value is in range; out-of-range values remain rejected.
